title: 2022 Review of Data-Driven Plasma Science
extended_summary:
This paper is a broad review of data-driven plasma science (DDPS), surveying how data science and machine learning are being applied across plasma research and technology. Rather than evaluating a specific intervention or educational program, it synthesizes advances in data reduction, dimensionality reduction, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, visualization, workflow automation, and database infrastructure as they relate to plasma science.

The paper is authored by a large international group of plasma and computational science researchers and is organized into topical sections covering fundamental data science, laboratory plasma experiments, magnetic confinement fusion, inertial confinement fusion, space and astronomical plasmas, industrial plasma technologies, and plasma-related databases. Across these areas, the authors describe how large data streams, machine learning, and high-performance computing can accelerate analysis, modeling, optimization, and control.

The main conclusion is that DDPS is still an emerging field, but one with significant promise for improving scientific discovery and operational efficiency in plasma science and technology. The paper argues that progress depends on better data curation, trustworthy reduction and surrogate methods, resilient workflows, and tighter integration between AI/ML techniques and domain physics. It does not report an empirical study, participant outcomes, or any K-12 educational implementation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a broad review article on data-driven plasma science, not an empirical study of K-12 educational intervention, student learning, or implementation artifacts. It does not evaluate Khanmigo or any AI tutoring system in an educational setting, so there is no clear study methodology relevant to the requested topic.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no direct evidence of impact on K-12 science learning outcomes, engagement, or implementation. The paper is domain-relevant only in the sense of discussing AI/data science generally, but it provides no measurable educational effect.
